title: General Psychology
topics: What psychology studies and how it works

items.q: Phenotype may be defined as
o: the observable characteristics produced by genes acting with the surroundings
the consistency of a test in giving similar scores on repeated occasions
the smallest change in a stimulus that a person can notice
the cell that carries electrochemical signals through the nervous system
items.s: Phenotype: the observable characteristics produced by genes acting with the surroundings. The other options describe Difference threshold, Reliability, Neuron.

items.s: Memory: the system that encodes, retains and later brings back information. The other options describe Sensory adaptation, Insomnia, Receptor.

items.q: Tolerance may be defined as
o: a design that records whether two attributes vary together without manipulating either

the failure to see a new use for an object because of its usual purpose
items.s: Tolerance: the need for a larger dose to produce an effect a smaller dose once gave. The other options describe Correlational study, Functional fixedness, Storage.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Standardisation?

items.s: Standardisation: the establishing of uniform procedures and norms so that scores can be compared. The other options describe Operant conditioning, Neuron, Consciousness.

items.s: Rationalisation: the invention of a respectable reason to cover a motive one does not wish to admit. The other options describe Colour blindness, Heredity, Figure and ground.

items.s: Reinforcement: a consequence that makes the behaviour before it more likely to recur. The other options describe Punishment, Illusion, Conditioned stimulus.
